Re-epithelization: Absence of epithelial proliferation in ≥ 70% of the tissue.
Granulation: Immature and inflammatory tissue in ≥ 70% of the tissue.
Angiogenesis: Absence of angiogenesis, presence of congestion, hemorrhage, and edema.

Re-epithelization: Poor epidermal organization in ≥ 60% of the tissue.
Granulation: Sparse immature and inflammatory tissue in ≥ 60% of the tissue.
Angiogenesis: 1–2 vessels per site, edema, hemorrhage, and congestion.

Re-epithelization: Incomplete epidermal organization in ≥ 40% of the tissue.
Granulation: Moderate remodeling in ≥ 40% of the tissue.
Angiogenesis: 3–4 vessels per site, moderate edema, and congestion.

Re-epithelization: Moderate epithelial proliferation in ≥ 60% of the tissue.
Granulation: Layer of coarse granulation and well-formed collagen matrix in ≥ 60% of the tissue.
Angiogenesis: 5–6 vessels per site, slight edema, and congestion.

Re-epithelization: Complete epidermal remodeling in ≥ 80% of the tissue.
Granulation: Complete tissue organization in ≥ 80% of the tissue.
Angiogenesis: More than seven vessels per site arranged vertically toward the epithelial surface.
